subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@averyanalytics.com>, Samir Khan <samir@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling next steps

Hi Jordan / Samir —

Thanks again for the call today — great overview of Avery's ingestion pipeline and the types of multi-step transformations you run on customer documents. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: surface high-precision structured outputs (JSON invoice + line items) from messy PDFs and semi-structured emails, with an automated retry path for tool/function calls when schema validation fails.
- Success metric: >95% JSON schema compliance on production prompt-set (sample size = 1k documents), and <2s median additional latency for function/tool calls under expected traffic.

Recommended quick plan (mutual action plan):
1) You share a 50–100 doc sample (anonymized) + the current JSON schema we should target.
2) We run an initial model-fit eval across two model configs (see recommendations below) and return: schema compliance, token cost estimate, and failing case examples.
3) If results look good, we run a 1k eval and propose a rollout path (canary via Redwood routing + automated fallback).

Initial model recommendations for this workload:
- rw-llama2-13b-8k-quant (balanced accuracy & cost; strong structured-output heuristics)
- rw-qa-7b-toolcall (optimized for tool/function calling — lower token cost, slightly higher hallucination risk on edge cases)

Tool/function calling & structured output notes:
- We'll enforce JSON schema compliance in the eval harness (schema validator step after model response).
- Retry policy we recommend for production: 2 retries with incremental prompt-context adjustments (shorter system instruction + hinting on failing fields).
- We'll capture KV/cache patterns and per-call latency in the benchmark so you can gauge production SLO impact.

Attachments included: a sample prompt set (avery_prompt_set.jsonl), benchmark template (model_benchmark_summary.csv), and eval instructions (redwood_eval_instructions.pdf).

Next steps: can you upload the sample docs to the Drive link I shared and drop a quick note about the exact schema version you want validated? I can have a first-pass eval back to you by Monday EOD PT.

Cheers,

---
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan@averyanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side before we upload the sample set: 

- Schema: we have two adjacent schema versions (v2 and v2.1). v2.1 adds optional tax_breakdown and vendor_normalized_name; we'd like both validated but pass criteria should target v2.
- JSON schema compliance definition: strict field types + presence of line_items array with at least description, qty, unit_price.
- Latency: our core SLA is 99th < 400ms for read-only ops; for tool-calling pipeline we can tolerate up to 2s on retries but would like to understand cost impacts.

Also: curious how you validate structured output when the model returns malformed JSON — do you prefer the model to return a single JSON blob or a JSON-wrapped text area that you post-process? We have a few multi-line OCR artifacts and sometimes the model splits tokens awkwardly.

Uploading a 100-doc sample to your Drive in the next 90 minutes. Please confirm if we should include OCR confidence scores as part of the document metadata.

—Jordan
Head of Product, Avery Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@averyanalytics.com>, Samir Khan <samir@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling next steps

Jordan — thanks for the notes and for uploading the sample. I pulled the files and ran a quick sanity pass. Couple of things and an initial plan: 

1) Schema strategy: we will validate against v2 as the primary pass and flag optional v2.1 fields separately (classification tag on failures). That gives you a hard pass/fail baseline while still tracking the new fields.

2) Malformed JSON handling: our eval harness has two modes — parser-first and model-first.
   - Parser-first: run a strict JSON parser on the model output; if it fails, we trigger a guided-retry prompt to the same model with 2 retries (recommended).
   - Model-first: attempt a best-effort parse with fuzzy heuristics and a downstream normalizer. This increases recall but adds complexity.

For this workload I recommend parser-first + 2 retries (Rishi will run the initial eval with those settings). That gives predictable compliance while keeping retry cost bounded.

3) Recommended eval config (we'll run both configs in parallel):
   - Config A (accuracy-focused): rw-llama2-13b-8k-quant, structured_response enforcement on, parser-first, retries=2, max_tokens=1024, temp=0.0
   - Config B (cost-focused): rw-qa-7b-toolcall, structured_response enforcement on, parser-first, retries=2, max_tokens=512, temp=0.0

4) Observability & artifacts we'll return: per-example schema result, token count, latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), examples that required retries, and a short set of prompt tweaks that improved parsing.

Attachments: I pushed an initial benchmark CSV and a short prompt-set (avery_prompt_set.jsonl) with annotations.

Rishi / Sean — can you run a first-pass eval on this sample (100 docs) and share the results by EOD Tuesday? Focus on: schema compliance rate per-config, top 10 failure modes, and avg token cost per doc.

Jordan / Samir — if you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min sync Wednesday to walk results and next steps.

Best,

---
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

P.S. OCR confidence scores are helpful; please include them as metadata if available.
